_comment: CAIOS additions to the dashboard's English strings. Deep-merged over vendor/ai4-dashboard/src/assets/i18n/en.json by scripts/build-dashboard.sh, the same way caios.json is merged over _base.json. Keys here win. _comment keys are stripped on the way in, so notes in this file never reach the browser.
_comment_audience: WHO THIS IS WRITTEN FOR. Medical and neuroscience academics, not engineers. They have not heard of Nomad, they do not know what a control plane is, and a node count tells them nothing except how small the thing is today. Every sentence here should survive being read by a clinician-scientist who has never deployed anything. tests/test_home_page.py enforces the vocabulary ban and the em-dash ban; both are easy to reintroduce by accident.

HOME.EYEBROW: CAIOS. Canadian Artificial Intelligence Operating System
HOME.HEADLINE: Research AI infrastructure,
HOME.DECK: Somewhere for medical and neuroscience groups to build, train and use AI models without handing anything to a commercial service. Work through a browser, or write your own code.
HOME.THESIS: Train on data that never leaves the hospital, or the country.
HOME._comment_figure_hero: The hero motif is a series of imaging slices, drawn as outlines rather than as anything resembling a real scan. It is a reference to what the platform is used for, not a claim about a particular study.

FIGURE.HERO-ALT: An abstract series of medical imaging slices, one of them highlighted.

SERVERLESS.TITLE: Publish a model that costs nothing while nobody is using it.
SERVERLESS.BODY: Make a model available for your group to use, and between requests it holds nothing at all. That lets you keep far more within reach than you could afford to keep running.
SERVERLESS.FIGURE-ALT: A timeline: nothing running, a short burst of activity, nothing running again.

FEDERATED.TITLE: Train across hospitals without moving their data.
FEDERATED.BODY: Each site trains on the records it holds and shares only what it learned. In our own study across three sites, the shared model came close to what pooling everything would have reached, and no site saw another's patients.
FEDERATED.FIGURE-ALT: Accuracy over ten rounds. The shared model reaches 0.853, above the best single site at 0.806, close to 0.865 for pooling everything.
FEDERATED.FIGURE-CAPTION: Ten rounds, one held out test set.

LLM.TITLE: A language model that reads clinical text without sending it anywhere.
LLM.BODY: Run an open language model on your own hardware and use it as you would any assistant, in a chat window or from your own scripts. Nothing you type reaches an outside service.
LLM.FIGURE-ALT: Notes and a reply, both inside a marked boundary, with the way out to an outside service crossed through.

NO-CODE.TITLE: Start without writing anything.
NO-CODE.BODY: Choose a model, fill in a short form, and a few minutes later it is running at your own address, ready to use.
NO-CODE.FIGURE-ALT: A short form with four fields and a submit button.

LOW-CODE.TITLE: Bring it into the work you already do.
LOW-CODE.BODY: Anything you set up gets its own address and key. Send it a scan, a recording or a passage of text from a script, and read the answer back.
LOW-CODE.FIGURE-ALT: A panel showing an address and a hidden access key.

HIGH-CODE.TITLE: Or work as deeply as you like.
HIGH-CODE.BODY: A full workspace runs beside your data, with the notebooks and tools your group already uses. The study behind this page was written exactly that way.
HIGH-CODE.FIGURE-ALT: A notebook with three cells, the middle one running.

CLOSING.TITLE: See what is available.
CLOSING.NOTE: The catalogue is open to read. Anything you create belongs to your own account once you sign in.
CLOSING.LAB: PACS Lab, as a platform for medical and neuroscience research.
CLOSING.STACK: AI4OS, an open source stack for research computing.
